prose.headline: Corsair is breaking down: short $12.79, target $10.97 by Oct 27, wrong on a close over $13.45.
story: Corsair lost its footing this week. It broke the rising support line, lost the 20-day on Oct 14 and then the 50-day on Friday, closing at $12.79 after a 3.4% drop on 0.85× normal volume. The mid-October poke over the 40-day high failed straight back, the classic upthrust, and there is no support within reach below: the next real level is the 38% retracement at $10.97. The bigger trend is still up, 97% in six months, which is exactly why a crack like this has room to run.

Momentum is rolling: RSI slipped to 45 from 50 and MACD has dropped under its signal, so the push is fading. Price sits under the VWAP since the last earnings at $12.85 and under the 20-day VWAP at $13.53, so recent buyers are underwater, and the busiest price at $13.56 is now overhead supply. Over the last month it is down 5.3%.
prose.play: Short it at $12.79. The objective is the 38% retracement at $10.97 by Oct 27. A daily close over $13.45, the 2-session high, says the break failed and I'm wrong. The desk's own strategy already owns it and stays long; this card takes the other side.

prose.headline: Park Hotels: buy at $15.91, objective $16.79 by Oct 23; a close under the 20-day at $15.37 ends it.
story: Park Hotels reclaimed its 20-day and 50-day averages together on Oct 15 and kept going, closing at $15.91 a step below the fresh 52-week high of $16.38. The swings are clean, higher highs and higher lows, and the 20-day at $15.37 now sits right under the price as the floor. Above, the weekly swing high at $16.15 and the high itself are all that stand between it and open air. ADX at 13 says the trend is young, not tired.

The reclaim came with buyers: 1.83× normal volume on a 1.2% gain and on-balance volume rising. MACD is above zero and above its signal with the gap widening, and RSI is 61, up from 58, so there is room before it runs hot. It has outrun 92% of stocks over six months, up 39%, and the profit swing to $47.0M from a $5.0M loss gives the move a reason. Price is above the VWAP since the last earnings at $15.30.

prose.headline: Insperity is a buy at $51.38 with the 50-day under it; target $54.94 by Oct 22, out below $50.31.
story: Insperity spent September and early October basing, shook out the weak hands with a quick undercut early in the month, and has been rising since: three of its last four swings were higher. Friday it retested the 50-day at $50.31 and held, a session after holding the 20-day, and closed at $51.38. The busiest price at $50.65 and the VWAP since the last earnings at $50.60 sit right under it, a thick floor. The weekly swing high at $54.94 is the ceiling to reach, with the 52-week high at $55.90 behind it.

MACD crossed up on Oct 8 and has pushed above zero, its gap with the signal widening, while RSI ticks up to 59 from 57: momentum is rebuilding, not stretched. Volume was a touch above normal at 1.18×. Six-month strength is big, up 78% and ahead of 97% of stocks, though over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 3.5 points. The divergence scan shows two warnings, the main thing against it.

story: Macerich topped at $26.68 in late July and has been distributing ever since: it trades under both its 10-week and 30-week averages, and the 50-day at $23.29 is falling and sits right on top of Friday's close at $22.96. The three-touch support line near $22.63 has given way. The bounce off the early-October undercut reclaimed the 20-day, but that is a daily bounce inside a weekly downtrend, and the first target below is the 2-session low at $22.36.

Friday's dip came on 1.59× normal volume and on-balance volume is falling, so sellers are doing the work. RSI eased to 52 from 54 and MACD is still below zero, though above its signal. The divergence scan has two bearish readings. Price is under the VWAP since the last earnings at $23.42, and over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 13.1 points. story: ArcBest topped at $176.69 in June and has given back a big chunk since: it trades under its 10-week and 30-week averages, the 50-day at $134.00 is falling, and the last swing low gave way. Friday's 2.3% drop put it back on the 20-day at $129.50 and the bottom of the high-volume range at $128.35, both thin cushions. The next real floor is the 200-day at $122.40, the target. The September undercut of $125.60 that snapped back is the one bullish memory in the chart.

RSI slid to 47 from 54 and MACD is below zero; it sits above its signal only because the earlier drop was deeper. Volume was ordinary at 1.08× normal. Price is under the VWAP since the last earnings at $136.17 and under the busiest price at $135.41, so the volume overhead is all supply. Over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 20.7 points, and a swing to a $13.8M loss from a $25.8M profit, despite revenue up 15.9%, explains why.

story: Campbell's has been in a long markdown: down from $32.04 last November to a low of $18.60, with both the 50-day at $21.39 and the 200-day at $22.76 falling and the monthly average rolling over. It has won back only 9% of that drop. The bounce from the October undercut of $18.90 lifted it to $19.87, but it stalled under a resistance zone that starts at $20.28, and the unfilled gap at $19.19 sits just below as the target.

The bounce is running out of fuel: volume was soft at 0.82× normal on Friday's 0.2% gain, and RSI is flat at 47. MACD is below zero and only just over its signal. ADX at 34 says the downtrend still has strength. Everyone who bought since the last earnings is underwater, with that VWAP at $20.40, and over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 12.9 points. Profit rose to $124.0M from $66.0M, but revenue fell 4.4%, and the chart is trading the revenue.

prose.headline: Darling slipped under its 20-day; sell $61.36 toward $58.96 by Oct 21, and a close over $62.62 stops it.
story: Darling peaked at $69.98 in August and has been leaking lower since: it lost the 50-day in September and the 20-day on Oct 15, and the support line drawn under the summer lows is broken. Friday's 0.8% bounce stalled right at the 20-day at $61.53 and the busiest price at $61.58, which now act as a lid. The last swing low at $58.96 is the target, with the bottom of the high-volume range at $59.30 on the way down.

On-balance volume is falling and money flow shows a bearish divergence, so the bounce is not being bought. RSI ticked up to 47 from 45 and MACD is below zero, a hair above its signal: a pause in the selling, not a turn. Price is under the VWAP since the last earnings at $63.31; over the last month it is down 7.7%. Profit jumped to $387.3M from $12.7M, the reason the desk's own strategy wants it, and the reason this is a fast trade, not a long one.

story: Donnelley Financial Solutions finished a double bottom on Friday, closing at $51.81 after a 0.9% gain on 1.16× normal volume. The 50-day retest on Oct 13 and the 20-day retest on Oct 14 both held, the September spring under the 40-day low set the base, and the 20-day at $48.85, 50-day at $48.53 and 200-day at $47.04 are all rising. It has won back 78% of the drop from $56.26 to $36.11. The weekly swing high at $52.33 is the near hurdle and the recent swing high at $53.56 the target.

story: Hexcel has rebuilt higher highs and higher lows since the September spring under the 40-day low, the 20-day retest on Oct 14 held, and Friday's 0.4% gain came on 1.46× normal volume. The support zone from $87.12 to $88.59 sits right under the price; the VWAP since the last earnings at $93.04 is the target.

This is low conviction because the bigger picture fights it. It lost the 50-day on Aug 19 and that average, $91.39, is falling 7.6% over 20 days, with the 200-day at $90.45 just overhead. Weekly RSI, MACD and A/D show bearish divergences, and over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 17.5 points. In its favour: on-balance volume is rising, MACD crossed up on Oct 1, RSI is 58, up from 57, and profit jumped to $49.3M from $13.5M. The weak point: at $90.22 it is above the desk's $89.49 cap, so buying now is chasing.

story: Kyndryl reclaimed the 20-day and the 50-day on Oct 15 and held them Friday on 1.57× normal volume, the weight of buyers absorbing supply. The VWAP since the last earnings at $12.63 is the floor, the busiest price at $13.16 sits right at the close, and the falling 200-day at $14.15 is the target.

The weak point: at $13.21 it is above the desk's $12.48 cap, so buying here is chasing.

prose.headline: Sonic Automotive's bounce stalls under the weekly high; sell $63.61 toward $60.58 by Oct 21, cover over $65.19.
story: Sonic Automotive has fallen from its $113.67 high on Jul 29 to a low of $54.11. The damage is everywhere: it lost the 50-day on Aug 3, and that average at $71.27 is falling 16.2% over 20 days. The 200-day at $73.25 and the earnings VWAP at $72.73 are well overhead, and the weekly chart is below both its averages. Price has broken down through its long support line. The bounce has run into the weekly swing high at $64.22, and the busiest price at $60.58 is the target below.

Three bearish divergences, including weekly RSI and money flow, say the bounce is weak. The three-month gap to the S&P 500 is a deep 36.8 points. This is a low-conviction call because the bounce has some footing: the 20-day was reclaimed on Oct 15, on-balance volume is rising, MACD crossed up on Oct 5, RSI is flat at 45, and profit swung to $57.4M from a $45.6M loss.
prose.play: Short at $63.61. Target $60.58, the busiest price, by Oct 21. I'm wrong on a daily close above $65.19, Friday's high. The desk's strategy is long and queued to buy a down day; this card takes the other side, small.

prose.headline: Sunstone: long $11.83, the $12.34 high back in play by Oct 23, void on a close under $11.50.
story: Sunstone Hotel Investors keeps its structure intact: price is above the 50-day exponential average, the 20-day was retested on Oct 12 and held, and the 50-day retest on Oct 8 held too. Friday it touched a fresh 52-week high at $12.34 and closed at $11.83, back under the weekly swing high at $11.95. The August spring under the 40-day low was the low of this run, and the 20-day at $11.34 and 50-day at $11.16 are both rising beneath it.

The catch is Friday's tape: 4.92× normal volume on a 0.3% dip, with on-balance volume pointing down, so some holders sold into the high, and an early-October upthrust shows the ceiling has bitten before. Against that, MACD is above zero and above its signal with the gap widening, and RSI at 68, down from 70, has cooled a touch without breaking. Up 23% in six months, ahead of 84% of stocks, with profit at $26.0M against $10.8M on revenue up 6.7%. The weak point: at $11.83 it is above the desk's $11.67 buy cap, so buying now is chasing.
prose.play: Buy at $11.83. The objective is the $12.34 high by Oct 23. A daily close under $11.50, the 2-session low, means Friday's selling won and I'm out. The desk has the same side queued lower, at or under $11.67.

story: Stanley Black & Decker is carving higher highs and higher lows again. An early-October spring undercut the 40-day low and snapped back, the support line near $86.63 is intact, and on Oct 15 the 20-day at $90.09 was retested and held. The support zone runs from $89.19 to $90.79 right under the price. The work is overhead: the weekly swing high at $93.37, the falling 50-day at $94.01 and the VWAP since the Jul 29 earnings at $94.53, with the recent swing high at $95.16 as the target.

Momentum has turned: MACD crossed up on Oct 1 and is closing the gap to zero, and RSI is steady at 55. Volume was 1.10× normal on a 0.3% dip, unremarkable, but on-balance volume is still pointing down, the main thing against it. Its weekly trend is bullish. Six months up 30%, ahead of 88% of stocks, the 200-day at $84.61 is rising, and profit more than tripled to $351.3M from $101.9M. Over three months it is 2.8 points ahead of the S&P 500.

story: Stryker has been in markdown since the $392.55 high last October and has won back only 22% of the slide to $267.00. It lost the 50-day on Aug 31 and has stayed under it; that average sits at $299.90 and is falling 6.4% over 20 days, with the 200-day at $326.60 falling too. On the weekly chart it is below both the 10-week and 30-week averages, and the monthly price is under a falling 10-month average at $324.02. A long falling resistance line caps the bigger picture.

This is a low-conviction call, and the bounce is why: the September spring under $270.85 has lifted it, the 20-day was retested on Oct 14 and held, and Friday's 0.5% gain came on 1.44× normal volume with on-balance volume rising. RSI is 59, up from 58, and MACD crossed up on Sep 28 though it is still below zero. Money flow shows a hidden bearish divergence on the weekly. Over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 10.5 points, and the VWAP since the last earnings at $301.24 and the weekly swing high at $301.58 sit just above.

story: monday.com fell 4.2% on Friday and stopped on the 50-day at $88.60, which held, two sessions after the 20-day retest on Oct 14 also held. The structure is intact: price is above the 50-day exponential average, the 30-week average is rising and the weekly chart sits above both its 10-week and 30-week averages. The busiest price at $87.22 is just under the close, and the weekly swing high at $95.46 is the ceiling to reach.

On-balance volume is rising with the price, so the dip came without real distribution, and volume was only 1.03× normal. MACD crossed up on Oct 8 and is above zero, steady over its signal; RSI eased to 55 from 60. It is up 39% in six months, ahead of 92% of stocks, and 14.9 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. What argues against it: the divergence scan carries two warning readings, and it has won back only 22% of the drop from $210.50 to $57.50, so this is a recovery, not a new leg.

The late-September spring under the 40-day low turned it, and the last two swings were higher after two lower. The 200-day at $63.68 sits under it as the line in the sand. story: Intuit is a daily bounce inside a weekly downtrend, and the bounce is the trade. The VWAP since the last earnings at $314.62 is the floor, and the busiest price at $343.93 is the magnet overhead.

prose.headline: Centene: long $69.16 after its new high, objective $73.46 by Oct 23, wrong below $67.98.
story: Centene touched a 52-week high at $71.21 on Friday, then gave back 1.9% to close at $69.16, a step under the double-bottom breakout level and weekly swing high at $69.63. The structure is intact above the 50-day exponential average, the 20-day retest on Oct 9 and the 50-day retest on Oct 12 both held, and the top of the high-volume range at $67.98 is the floor under the price. The 200-day at $54.15 is rising and the 30-week average is climbing.

The giveback came on 0.90× normal volume while on-balance volume kept rising, so it reads as profit-taking rather than selling. MACD has been above its signal since the Oct 6 cross and holds over zero, with the gap starting to narrow. RSI cooled to 62 from 69. The turnaround is the catalyst: profit of $1,091.0M against a $253.0M loss, revenue up 9.9%, and an 81% six-month gain, ahead of 97% of stocks. Against it: the stochastic is stretched at 93, and only 31% of stocks are above their 50-day.

prose.headline: Coty broke its swing high: long $3.20, objective $3.38 by Oct 22, exit on a close under $3.11.
story: Coty is up 30.1% in a month and has turned its chart: two higher swings after two lower, a close above the last swing high at $3.09, and both the 20-day and 50-day retests holding, on Oct 5 and Oct 8. The 20-day at $2.78 and 50-day at $2.77 are rising, and the support zone from $3.04 to $3.11 now sits under the price. The resistance zone that starts at $3.38 is the objective, and it has won back 52% of the drop from $4.47 to $1.82.

On-balance volume is rising and the daily A/D shows a bullish divergence; price is moving easily on light volume, 0.94× normal, so there is little in the way. RSI is steady at 75, hot. It is 15.7 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. The weak points: at 3.5 daily ranges above the 50-day it is stretched, the business is not helping, a $408.1M loss against $405.7M on revenue down 1.3%, and earnings drew a weak reaction.

story: Molina Healthcare got back over the 50-day at $199.40 on Oct 12, the same day a 20-day retest held, and the early-October spring under the 40-day low marked the turn. The weekly picture is in markup: above the 10-week and 30-week averages, with a rising 200-day at $183.60. The VWAP since the last earnings at $200.47 is the floor, and the 52-week high at $244.89 from Jul 14 is the objective, past the weekly swing high at $214.36.

But a mid-October upthrust over the 40-day high failed, Friday fell 2.4% on 1.11× normal volume, on-balance volume is pointing down, and the scan shows hidden bearish divergences. RSI fell to 58 from 65. The business is the drag: profit fell to $60.0M from $255.0M, revenue is down 4.8%, and it trails the S&P 500 by 12.6 points over three months.

story: Perrigo has been climbing a clean staircase, higher highs and higher lows, and Friday's 0.9% gain closed it above the last swing high at $15.69. The 20-day retest on Oct 9 held, the 50-day at $14.23 is rising 13.6% over 20 days, and the VWAP since the last earnings at $14.18 is well below. It has won back 56% of the slide from $22.48 to $9.23, and the 52-week high at $22.02 is the target; the space in between has little supply.

Three hidden bullish divergences, including the daily A/D, say dips are being bought, and on-balance volume is rising. RSI is 71, up from 70, warm but not rolling. The profit swing is the catalyst: $74.5M against an $8.4M loss, even with revenue down 3.2%. Over three months it has beaten the S&P 500 by 54.2 points. Against it: 3.5 daily ranges above the 50-day is stretched, and the stock has a weak October record.

prose.headline: Doximity: buy $30.97 alongside the desk, aim at $34.22 by Oct 27, a close under $29.62 breaks it.
story: Doximity is in a steep recovery: higher highs and higher lows, the 20-day at $28.36 climbing 10.2% over 20 days and the 50-day at $26.78 rising under it. The last 20-day retest, on Sep 29, held, and MACD crossed up the next day and is still above its signal. ADX at 40 says the trend is strong. The busiest price at $34.22 is the magnet above, past the weekly swing high at $31.86.

Friday was a wobble: a 1.7% dip on 1.29× normal volume, with on-balance volume pointing down, and RSI cooled to 66 from 70. That, plus 3.3 daily ranges of stretch above the 50-day, is why this is Medium, not higher. The bigger frame cuts both ways: it has run 42.5% in three months, 39.7 points ahead of the S&P 500, yet it is only 43% of its 52-week high at $71.37. Profit fell to $24.3M from $53.3M while revenue grew 7.3%.
prose.play: Buy at $30.97. My objective is the busiest price at $34.22 by Oct 27. A daily close under $29.62, the 5-session low, says the recovery cracked and I'm wrong. The desk bought it on Friday, so this card agrees with the desk.

story: Becton Dickinson set a 52-week high at $195.99 on Friday before easing 1.0% to $191.75. The swings are higher highs and higher lows, and Oct 9 did triple duty: the 20-day and 50-day retests both held and MACD crossed up the same day. Beneath it, the 200-day at $164.10 keeps rising. The weekly swing high at $193.07 is the near hurdle, and past the highs the objective is a measured move to $200.29.

Friday's dip came on 0.87× normal volume and on-balance volume kept rising, so the move is moving easily with little supply. RSI eased to 64 from 68. The three-month lead over the S&P 500 is 21.3 points. Against it: a broken support line, a stretched stochastic at 92, and profit down to $377.0M from $574.0M even with revenue up 5.4%.

story: BlackRock took back the 50-day at $1,106.00 on Oct 15, the same day a 20-day retest held, and Friday added 1.2% on 2.20× normal volume, the kind of follow-through that says institutions are in. The structure is intact above the 50-day exponential average, the support line near $1,047.00 is intact, and the VWAP since the last earnings at $1,106.61 is now under the price. It has won back 72% of the drop from $1,220.00 to $917.40, and the weekly swing high at $1,171.89 is next.

On-balance volume is rising, MACD crossed up on Sep 25 and is now above zero with the gap widening, and RSI rose to 64 from 61. The business is strong: revenue up 30.6% and profit $1,914.0M against $1,593.0M. Against it: negative headlines, and the 52-week high at $1,209.89 set a year ago is a reminder that this is a recovery, not yet a breakout.

story: Church & Dwight reclaimed the 20-day on Oct 5 and the 50-day on Oct 12, and both reclaims held. Profit edged up to $202.8M from $191.0M on revenue up 1.6%; it is a staples name that is 4.0 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. The weak points: 3.5 daily ranges above the 50-day, and the weekly stage reads as a possible top, so this is Medium conviction with a tight stop.

The weekly swing high at $135.46 is the only nearby lid; above it, the road runs to the one-year high at $158.20.

The fundamentals are doing the lifting: profit up to $550.3M from $411.4M on revenue up 5.2%. Against it: the August upthrust over the 40-day high is the last time this area turned it back, and credit markets are nervous.

story: DiamondRock Hospitality rose 1.1% on Friday on 1.94× normal volume to $13.42, closing in on the 52-week high and weekly swing high at $13.79 from Aug 3. It reclaimed the 20-day on Oct 8 and retested the 50-day on Oct 12, holding both, and the 20-day at $12.61 and 200-day at $11.07 are rising. The chart has moved into a breakout stage. Past the high, a measured move points to $14.14.

On-balance volume is rising and MACD is above zero with the gap widening; RSI rose to 69 from 67. Profit more than doubled to $90.5M from $40.8M on revenue up 4.1%, and it is up 27% in six months, ahead of 87% of stocks. The warnings: the daily A/D and weekly money flow both show divergences, and the stochastic is at 80, so it is Medium conviction.

prose.headline: Encore Capital pulled in quietly: buy $101.68, objective $105.86 by Oct 21, a close under $99.30 and I'm out.
story: Encore Capital set a 52-week high at $105.98 on Oct 14 and has eased back to $101.68 since, on very light volume: Friday's 0.9% dip came on just 0.50× normal. The swings are higher highs and higher lows, the 20-day and 50-day retests on Oct 12 both held, and the support zone from $97.27 to $99.30 sits right under the price with the 200-day at $80.93 far below and rising. The objective is $105.86, the old support line now overhead.

On-balance volume is rising and the daily A/D shows hidden bullish divergences, so the pullback is a rest. MACD crossed up on Oct 7 and holds above zero, though the gap is narrowing; RSI eased to 56 from 58. Collections are paying: revenue up 11.3%, profit $64.0M against $58.7M. The weak point: the weekly swing high at $102.97 comes first, and the room to it is smaller than the distance to the stop. The reversal candles at the high and two warning divergences are why this is not Top.

story: Employers Holdings cleared a descending triangle two sessions ago and the breakout retest held. Friday it rose 1.5% to $51.21, just under the weekly swing high at $51.48 and within reach of the 52-week high at $52.59 from Jul 30, which is the target. The 20-day and 50-day retests on Oct 8 both held, the late-September spring under the 40-day low set the base, and the 200-day at $45.50 is rising.

On-balance volume is rising and two bullish divergences back the breakout. MACD crossed up on Oct 2 and is above zero; RSI jumped to 68 from 63. Volume was 0.90× normal. Against it: over three months it trails the S&P 500 by 1.2 points, the daily A/D gives a warning, and the July upthrust at the highs shows sellers have defended this area before.

story: National Beverage climbed back over the 20-day and the 50-day together on Oct 12 and both reclaims held. Friday it rose 1.9% on 1.33× normal volume to $34.96, above the 200-day at $33.54 and into a breakout stage. It has won back 65% of the slide from $38.21 to $28.97, and the resistance zone that starts at $37.50 is the objective, past the weekly swing high at $35.57.

The divergence evidence is lopsided: two bullish and two hidden bullish readings, with the daily A/D and money flow agreeing, and on-balance volume rising. MACD crossed up on Oct 8 and the gap is widening; RSI rose to 72 from 70. Relative to the S&P 500 it is 9.4 points better over three months. Against it: at 3.6 daily ranges above the 50-day it is as stretched as it has been in a year, and there is no support within reach below.
